title: Recursion and Advanced Functions knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Recursion and Advanced Functions”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Recursive function calls” under lesson 65, “Recursion and Advanced Functions”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Recursion and Advanced Functions”?
options: Separate a function’s exit status from any data it prints.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
questions.answer_key: Separate a function’s exit status from any data it prints.
questions.explanation: Separate a function’s exit status from any data it prints. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Recursion and Advanced Functions”?
options: Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
